subject: Request: temporary burst quota exception for open-enrollment spike
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@horizonhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.com>, Horizon Health IT Team <it@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary burst quota exception for open-enrollment spike

Hi Karthik / Laura,

We're ramping up for open enrollment (starts 2025-07-01) and expect a large short-lived surge in inference traffic for eligibility checks and benefits summarization. Our current Dedicated instance will hit the standard burst quota and throttling thresholds.

Is there an option to request a temporary exception to the burst limit (elastic burst window) that would allow higher token throughput for ~72 hours during the first week of enrollment? If necessary, we can sign a one-off addendum and provide a forecast of peak qps. The goal is to avoid 503s and keep latency below 200ms p95 for members hitting the benefits assistant.

Key asks:
- Temporary increase to burst limit from 3x to 6x (for a 72-hour window)
- Explicit fairness/throttling policy during the window so we know how you prioritize traffic
- Any required SLAs or credits if throttling causes errors

I've attached our estimate and the initial procurement note. Happy to jump on a call this week.

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Product Operations
Horizon Health
[Attachment: open-enroll-traffic-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Evan Brooks <evan@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary burst quota exception for open-enrollment spike

Evan — thanks for the heads up and the estimate. This is the kind of production event we expect to support, and we can make a short-term exception but need to align on guardrails.

Quick summary of what we can offer and next steps:
- Temporary burst window: can approve a 72-hour elevated burst that increases your per-customer burst factor from 3x -> 5x by default. We can entertain 6x but would need approval from Capacity and Finance (higher surcharge).
- Fairness & throttling: during the window we apply a weighted fairness policy that favors pinned/priority API keys and customer-configured routes; unpinned requests may see progressive token-rate throttling.
- Monitoring & alerts: we'll enable an elevated monitoring policy and forward token-level traces; we'll also create a short-lived trace-based SLO dashboard.
- SLA/credits: we can offer a service credit for any sustained p95 latency > 400ms or error rates > 2% during the window, capped at X% of monthly committed spend. Exact credit language requires a one-off addendum.

Can you confirm: (1) the exact 72-hour UTC window you want; (2) whether you want priority for specific API keys/routes (and list them); and (3) whether Horizon is willing to accept a temporary surcharge for the increased capacity?

I'll loop in Marcus from Capacity to confirm physical GPU availability and the pricing deltas. If you want, we can prepare a one-page addendum and DocuSign.

—Karhtik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_exception_form.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary burst quota exception for open-enrollment spike

On Mon, Jun 16, 2025 at 11:03 AM karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> Karhtik — thanks for the heads up and the estimate. This is the kind of production event we expect to support, and we can make a short-term exception but need to align on guardrails.
> 
> Quick summary of what we can offer and next steps:

We have capacity in us-west-2 for the requested week; 6x sustained is a hard ask but doable if Horizon pays the surcharge and agrees to the throttling/fairness policy. I'll coordinate node reservations and bump the burst config for their Dedicated pool.

Notes on implementation:
- We'll create a temporary rate-limit profile attached to their Dedicated cluster that increases token throughput and widens the per-request concurrency ceiling for the 72-hour window.
- The fairness policy will respect "priority_key" metadata; if not provided, we fallback to token-cost-based proportional fairness.
- We'll also enable stricter prefix cache sharing to reduce duplicate compute during the event.

Laura — can you draft the addendum language (pricing delta + credit cap) and send to Procurement? I'll prepare the ops runbook (node reservations, monitoring links).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Capacity Manager, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Evan Brooks <evan@horizonhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, it@horizonhealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary burst quota exception for open-enrollment spike

Evan / team — following internal signoff, we can accommodate the temporary exception with the following proposed terms. I included the addendum and a link to a draft runbook.

Proposed exception (summary):
- Window: 2025-07-01T00:00:00Z through 2025-07-04T00:00:00Z (72 hours)
- Burst factor: standard 3x -> elevated 5x during window. 6x available with 15% surcharge on committed monthly spend (indicate acceptance in DocuSign).
- Fairness policy: priority_key-based weighted scheduling. Requests without priority_key will be metered by proportional token-cost weight; in extremis we apply progressive throttling (HTTP 429) per-client to maintain cluster health.
- Latency SLOs and credits: if sustained p95 > 400ms for more than 30 minutes, or error rate > 2% for more than 30 minutes, Horizon will be eligible for a pro-rated service credit up to 10% of the monthly committed fee for the period. Credit triggers require Redwood monitoring logs (we'll provide exported traces).
- Monitoring & ops: dedicated SLO dashboard, pager escalation to Redwood on-call for the window, pre-scheduled health checks every 6 hours.
- Implementation: Marcus will reserve nodes and apply a temporary rate-limit profile; Laura will send the addendum to Procurement.

Attachments and links: SLA_exception_form.pdf (please sign), proposed-burst-policy-2025-06.xlsx, runbook link: https://redwood.app/doc/HH-2025-06-burst-policy

Next steps for Horizon: please confirm (a) acceptance of the 5x window or request 6x with surcharge, (b) list of priority API keys/routes to pin, and (c) sign the addendum so we can schedule node reservation. We'll plan a 30-minute ops run-through (Marcus + Horizon IT) 48 hours before the window.

If you'd like a call now, I can put time on the calendar this week.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/HH-2025-06-burst-addendum]
